claim: For any three rank-one projective measurements of a qubit, represented by unoriented unit Bloch axes \(n_1,n_2,n_3\), define \(\bar S(r)=\frac13\sum_{j=1}^3 h((1+n_j\cdot r)/2)\) for pure-state Bloch vectors \(r\in S^2\), where \(h(p)=-p\log p-(1-p)\log(1-p)\), and let \(B_{\min}=\min_r\bar S(r)\), \(B_{\max}=\max_r\bar S(r)\). Then \(B_{\min}\le \frac23\log2\) and \(B_{\max}\ge \beta_*=h((1+1/\sqrt3)/2)=\frac12\log6-\frac{1}{2\sqrt3}\log(2+\sqrt3)\). Equality in either extremal inequality holds if and only if the three measurement bases are pairwise mutually unbiased, equivalently \(n_i\cdot n_j=0\) for \(i\ne j\). Thus the lower-bound and upper-bound assertions of Conjecture 1 in arXiv:1506.07709 are both true for \(N=2\) and \(L=3\).

correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs the exact Bloch probability law and reduces the entropy to H(s)=h((1+sqrt(s))/2). Its second derivative is strictly negative. For MUB axes the squared overlaps form a simplex, giving both exact extrema. For arbitrary axes, the lower inequality follows from an eigenstate input with rigidity. The upper inequality follows from an exact eight-sign average and tr(C^{-1})>=3 for the Gram matrix C, with separate treatment of singular frames; every equality condition is explicit. The checker corroborates identities but the universal result rests on the analytic proof.
